chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad bin Ali (who ascribed it to the Imam), saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Beware of branched lying. It was said to him: And what is branched lying? He said: That a man tells you a narration, and then you narrate it from other than the one who told it to you.

key_terms.الْكَذِبُ الْمُفْتَرَعُ: Branched lying; a specific form of deception in narration
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: He ascribed it (to a higher authority, typically the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of branched lying in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this definition of 'branched lying' (al-kadhib al-mufra') to highlight a subtle but critical error in hadith transmission where the narrator alters the attribution of a statement to a different source. This specific form of deception undermines the integrity of the isnad (chain of transmission) by creating a false link, which is particularly significant in Shia scholarship for verifying the authenticity of reports attributed to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Muhammed ibn Ali, that he ascribed it, saying: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:
Beware from branched lying. It was said to him: And what is branched lying. He said: That a man tells you a narration, and then you narrate it of other than the one who told it to you.
